Inter-Subject Correlation¶

neurora.isc_cal

Function Index¶

  • isc

  • isc_fmri

  • isc_fmri_roi

API Details¶

a module for calculating the inter-subject correlation based on neural data

neurora.isc_cal.isc(data, time_win=5, time_step=5, parallel=False, n_jobs=-1, backend='loky')¶

Calculate inter-subject correlation (ISC) for EEG-like data.

Parameters:

  • data (array_like, shape [n_subs, n_chls, n_ts]) –

    EEG-like neural data.

    n_subs, n_chls, and n_ts represent the number of subjects, channels, and time points, respectively.

  • time_win (int, default=5) – Time-window size in samples.

  • time_step (int, default=5) – Step size between adjacent time windows.

  • parallel (bool, default=False) – Whether to parallelize across subject pair × channel × time-window tasks.

  • n_jobs (int, default=-1) – Number of workers used when parallel=True. If n_jobs=-1, all available CPU cores will be used.

  • backend ({"loky", "threading"}, default="loky") – Joblib backend used when parallel=True.

Returns:

isc_results – ISC results.

The last dimension contains:

  • isc_results[…, 0] : r-value

  • isc_results[…, 1] : p-value

Return type:

ndarray, shape [n_pairs, n_chls, n_windows, 2]

Notes

ISC is computed for each unique pair of subjects.

neurora.isc_cal.isc_fmri(fmri_data, ksize=(3, 3, 3), strides=(1, 1, 1), parallel=False, n_jobs=-1, backend='loky')¶

Calculate inter-subject correlation (ISC) for fMRI data using searchlights.

Parameters:

  • fmri_data (array_like, shape [n_ts, n_subs, nx, ny, nz]) –

    fMRI data.

    n_ts, n_subs, nx, ny, and nz represent the number of time points, subjects, and spatial dimensions.

  • ksize (tuple or list of int, default=(3, 3, 3)) – Searchlight kernel size along x, y, and z axes.

  • strides (tuple or list of int, default=(1, 1, 1)) – Searchlight strides along x, y, and z axes.

  • parallel (bool, default=False) – Whether to parallelize across time point × subject pair × searchlight tasks.

  • n_jobs (int, default=-1) – Number of workers used when parallel=True. If n_jobs=-1, all available CPU cores will be used.

  • backend ({"loky", "threading"}, default="loky") – Joblib backend used when parallel=True.

Returns:

isc_results – fMRI searchlight ISC results.

The last dimension contains:

  • isc_results[…, 0] : r-value

  • isc_results[…, 1] : p-value

Return type:

ndarray, shape [n_ts, n_pairs, n_x, n_y, n_z, 2]

Notes

ISC is computed for each unique pair of subjects.

The NaN handling follows the original logic: for each time point, subject pair, and searchlight unit, the ISC is set to NaN if either subject’s searchlight vector contains NaN.

neurora.isc_cal.isc_fmri_roi(fmri_data, mask_data, parallel=False, n_jobs=-1, backend='loky')¶

Calculate inter-subject correlation (ISC) for fMRI data within an ROI.

Parameters:

  • fmri_data (array_like, shape [n_ts, n_subs, nx, ny, nz]) – fMRI data.

  • mask_data (array_like, shape [nx, ny, nz]) – ROI mask. Non-zero and finite voxels are included.

  • parallel (bool, default=False) – Whether to parallelize across time point × subject pair tasks.

  • n_jobs (int, default=-1) – Number of workers used when parallel=True. If n_jobs=-1, all available CPU cores will be used.

  • backend ({"loky", "threading"}, default="loky") – Joblib backend used when parallel=True.

Returns:

isc_results – fMRI ROI ISC results.

The last dimension contains:

  • isc_results[…, 0] : r-value

  • isc_results[…, 1] : p-value

Return type:

ndarray, shape [n_ts, n_pairs, 2]

Notes

ISC is computed for each unique pair of subjects.

The ROI voxel selection follows the original logic: voxels are included if the mask is non-zero and finite. fMRI NaNs are handled at the time point × subject pair level, where the corresponding ISC value becomes NaN if either subject’s ROI vector contains NaN.
